summary: First backend test run for Mobile Build Resolver. All 28 pytest cases PASSED against the live preview backend (which proxies live Redash / deployer / deployer-MCP / expo-MCP). Health, diagnose (known + unknown job), sensitive-field redaction, diagnose logs, expo lookup+builds (401 as expected), identity iOS/Android (validation + surfacing), keystore GET (+ invalid user_id 400) + DER-upload rejection, clear-asc preview & execute, testflight-retry, fingerprint lookup + bad-archive URL, force-regen platform validation + iOS/Android execution, PEM extract-upload-key + P8 encrypt (kubectl-missing surfaced gracefully, not 500), MCP deployer passthrough, and audit log writes -- all verified.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~700 lines and mixes routing + SQL constants + keystore-conversion helper (_convert_keystore_to_pem) + redaction. Consider splitting into routers/ (diagnose.py, keystore.py, creds.py, pem.py, mcp.py) and moving Q_* constants + _convert_keystore_to_pem into dedicated modules. Not blocking but future-proofing.

force_regen returns Redash's raw response including 'ok' and 'error' fields but no explicit status_code -- consider surfacing a normalised {reachable, status_code, error} shape for parity with deployer_client responses.
audit.log is fire-and-forget awaited; if Mongo is slow it will block the request. Consider background task (BackgroundTasks / asyncio.create_task with error logging) for destructive endpoints.
keystore_upload catches Exception broadly when computing auto_fingerprint (line 428) -- fine, but log the exception at WARN so operators can diagnose bad PEMs later.
redact_row only redacts top-level keys; if a nested dict ever carries these keys they will leak. Current queries never return nested JSON so this is theoretical.
seed_data_creation: none; used JOB=41b30fe6-9d40-4818-b76f-df7bac4858e7 which is a real stale job in Redash
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is fully green against live endpoints. The pytest file /app/backend/tests/test_backend.py is idempotent and safe to re-run (destructive endpoints only touch a known-stale test job). If a future run needs a fresh job_id, fetch one via `SELECT job_id FROM android_app_configs ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 3` through /api/diagnose or a manual Redash curl (REDASH_API_KEY in backend/.env). Frontend testing was explicitly out of scope.
